searchText: Making a thread. The main outcome I don't want, to be concrete, is that the usual outcome is lots of branches which need to be maintained for semi-indefinite time periods (weeks, months) until everything gets merged. I don't deeply care whether what we call the main thing we're testing "CFI" or "SFI", that's just a name. But having lots of branches is the real cost, and that I will continue to push back strongly against Lots of branches where exactly? In the spec or in clients? Or both? I don't want to deal with this in the specs. both And sorry, but 8015 is the worst excuse here it's absolutely trivial (it's been cited before) For readers, this is a [previous relevant thread](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1562403836105330819). In EELS we only merge SFI'd EIPs on the main branch, its not documented in the EIP process only in the EELS process. It should be documented in the EIP process. It feels like we can agree on doing in this in CL specs too? the problem is that they are exclusive in some cases: if we do add CFId features to the main spec branch that I DONT want to implement at all, then I am forced to implement the SFId features in a branch because I can't pass the testvectors. To be very clear here, I agree that the process is ambiguous at the moment and needs to be sharpened. I think there are some parallel friction points here wrt specs especially. One is that CFI'd EIPs being included in devnets are being chosen by very few people at times and forced into implementation. And another is that the specs (consensus) seems to merge into the main spec these CFI EIPs rather than only merge SFI EIPs into main spec. Correct me if I'm wrong on the consensus-specs side. > To me it is a no brainer that we must not merge into that next-fork-branch EIPs that are not SFId and EIPs that clients aren't forced to implement. On the execution-specs we don't merge anything that isn't SFI into the main spec. Each CFI EIP is implemented standalone on an `eips/bogota/eip-NNNN` branch and we have a github workflow that merges EIP branches together to create a devnet branch (`devnets/heze/3`, for example) – with humans sussing out any conflicts where EIPs interact. From this devnet branch we cut the test release for the devnets. So I think there is some disconnect between "something is CFI'd and we need to test it so it goes in this devnet" and "merging this spec into the actual fork". From the chatter on my end, it also feels like we need to 1) increase the bar for PFI, 2) increase the bar for CFI and 3) add a process for devnet inclusion after CFI. Whether adding a new label for this (TFI - testing for inclusion) or not, cc-ing this PR to add to the discussion: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12452 > On the execution-specs... Yes, very much this, I want the CL specs to behave like the EL specs Also to be clear, I'm not suggesting the way execution-specs does it is the "correct way". I mostly agree with all said here. I just think we should have one process perhaps on both specs side. Yeah, the part I agree with <@755590043632140352> on is that right now there's this gap of what do PFI/CFI/SFI practically mean, and there's this situation where things get CFI'd too easily for a scenario where it's likely by default to become required for testing Right, the issue is that > Yes, very much this, I want the CL specs to behave like the EL specs Has downsides we very much see So since this is the overall thrust, that's what I'm arguing against Yeah perhaps there isn't a need to "do things the same way" in both repos. But maybe at least decoupling CFI'd EIPs from "merging to the main spec" 🤔. I'm not sure the answer here tbh, I don't have enough context on the CL spec dev cycle. We should invite more CL devs to weigh in before making any decisions IMO. this is about more than CL devs, this is why my decision to post on ACD channel rather than <#598292067260825641>, I'd like to hear positions from every side as it involves the process for inclusion in forks A compromise that I'm open to but not really supportive of would be introducing a new directory for devnet specs, in the master branch. But that would still mean duplicate specs. I quite like the way things are in consensus-specs right now. I want to continue merging CFI'd specs (when they are ready & we're ready to start testing them) into the upgrade specs. This is the way we've done things in the past. `specs/<upgrade>`, `specs/_features/eipXXXX`, `specs/_devnets/<upgrade>-devnet-X` But I still think this will be complex & not worth it. yeah that's an interesting idea -- it means avoiding the proliferation of branches, but avoids premature CFI-oops-actually-SFI but not sure if overall worthwhile, sure <@199561711278227457> made a good point today that gating the CFI process / taking it with more weight than we have been could help here. In that sense anything that is CFI'd is now "on track" to be SFI unless testing proves with consensus across ACD that this isn't worth complexity or it causes x, y, z problems. And in that case, it would simplify our process on execution-specs side as well Yeah at least with this structure, a single PR could update all specs. Like update eip8198 and heze-devnet-3 at the same time. this is how i view cfi tbh we wouldn't need to upkeep all these branches and mega merge things into devnet branches, etc. and we can start merging CFI EIPs to specs as well Yes, personally I do also But it's clear that's not universal if we could merge CFI'd EIPs in EELS I think it would accelerate us, we have branching pain with the current EELS process And in this sense an EIP that was "weakly CFI'd" or "contentiously CFI'd" has no argument (quick slots has been getting this flack). You either speak up at the CFI time or you swallow the fact that you have to merge it to spec now and implement it. So I think it needs less ambiguity around what CFI means one point keeps coming up that I struggle with, is a CFI is a soft SFI? for me its not the case, we should be able to take our sunk cost bias out of decisions, EOF and Verkle are the outliers here if CFI is a soft SFI im happy but I'd like it to be defined as that I think in this stronger CFI gate, it would be a soft SFI. It has to be. otherwise we shouldn't merge to spec That's the whole ambiguity imo It does bring up a good point though that something like EIP-8037 springs up. Thankfully we were all onboard but an EIP that starts changing under our feet and becomes a trojan horse headliner (without being named one)... if it begins presenting testing problems and increasing surface area and complexity then it should be able to be DFI. But now we have some sunk cost energy well to climb out of and convince people to DFI. Isn't that more of a function of implementation/testing effort than per-se some label (PFI, CFI, SFI)? There were several sessions in Svalbard aroud it Yeah I guess so. And it will ideally be the exception to the rule that this happens too (EOF, for example). but it would present a fairly strong friction point I think after being in a devnet to remove so how do we wanna move forward? I can clearly see both sides are a bit unhappy here, someone will have to compromise. Right now what we have is the worst situation where we have 4 clients that have implemented an open PR without a test release and we launched a devnet that’s testing an open pr. This is messy as we can reference a specific version and we can’t say which other changes or commit hash we actually mean. I’d personally think that the final decision should be in the hand of cl spec maintainers. As they are the ones that are gonna keep this ship moving long term, and if they are unhappy, everyone will be unhappy imo. I’d personally prefer if Jihoon and Justin are taking an executive decision in this matter and settle however they see fit the process to move forward. let that be branches or devnet specific releases or keep to what they been doing now. I just wanna make sure we won’t get deadlocked in this place where we can’t make new releases because always someone is unhappy. Do we also have the issue of no champion for 8198? There are 5 approvals on the open PR but it's not merged bc we lack the right people being around for the process it seems. Yeah my pr adds barnabé and me as authors. we just need someone to merge it then 😅 once Carl approves it it can be merged. Already reached out to him it has to be the original author:/ That's probably my bad, I did not realise that the flow depended on being able to merge the EIP PRs quickly, or that the "official" champion should be an author too (I don't really care about the authorship) and Carl is currently less active, supports the effort but is not expected to be the champion. At this point I am fulfilling the champion role, and now Barnabas has done a ton as well (grateful 🙏 ) If there are any questions on 8198 always feel free to direct to me. All good! Just good to try to find the pain points and iron them out 🙂

From this devnet branch we cut the test release for the devnets.

So I think there is some disconnect between "something is CFI'd and we need to test it so it goes in this devnet" and "merging this spec into the actual fork".
